name: Overclave
manufacturer: Street lab (origin: former Helix Biosystems researcher)
description: An illicit CNS stimulant that targets the BCI's neural interface layer, flooding it with a synthetic adenosine antagonist and a proprietary SNT-excitatory compound. The result is a dramatic, dangerous increase in BCI processing speed — users describe seeing the world in frames, their augments responding to thoughts they haven't finished thinking. Overclave is the drug you take when you need to be faster than anything alive, knowing it might kill you.
effects: BCI processing speed increased 200-400% above baseline
Augmented reflexes operate in near-predictive mode — the chrome moves before conscious thought
Sensory augments process full-spectrum input simultaneously without lag
Time perception distorted — subjective experience slows dramatically
Complete suppression of fear and hesitation responses
side_effects: Cerebral hemorrhage risk: 12% per dose, rising with repeat use
Grand mal seizure during or after peak effect
Permanent neural pathway degradation with multiple uses
SNT interface scarring that permanently reduces BCI bandwidth
Death (estimated 4% single-dose mortality in compromised users)
cultural_context: Overclave is a last-resort drug on the Shelf — you take it when you're cornered, when the odds are impossible, when dying fast is better than dying slow. It has a mythology around it: stories of Shelf runners who took Redline and fought their way out of impossible situations. The reality is most people who use it regularly are dead within six months from neural bleed or heart failure. The name 'The Needle' comes from the sensation users report — a bright, thin line of clarity that feels like a needle through the center of your skull.
story_hooks: A Shelf enforcer has been using Overclave to maintain dominance in their territory — their BCI is visibly degrading, they're having micro-seizures, and they know they're dying. They want one last job done before they go, and they're paying everything they have.
Someone has begun distributing Overclave in Tier 3 disguised as a legitimate BCI performance supplement — the first deaths are being reported, and the manufacturer's trail leads somewhere unexpected
A combat medic who worked the Shelf has developed what they claim is an Overclave antidote — but testing it requires finding someone mid-dose, and the window is minutes
